articles.title: Anelis Assumpção mergulha no reggae em álbum com Alice Carvalho, Liniker, Tetê Espíndola e Thalma de Freitas | G1
articles.body:
Capa do álbum 'Anelis e o favo favorito', de Anelis Assumpção — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Novembro chega com o quinto álbum de estúdio de Anelis Assumpção , “Anelis e o favo favorito”. Invertendo a ordem habitual adotada pelo mercado fonográfico, o álbum é lançado primeiramente em LP – com vinil fabricado na cor mel, em afinidade com o título – e somente em 30 de novembro ficará disponível em edição digital nos aplicativos de áudio.

Em “Anelis e o favo favorito”, a artista dá um mergulho mais profundo na praia do reggae – gênero recorrente na discografia da cantora – em álbum que flerta com a cultura do Sound System e que apresenta repertório essencialmente inédito e autoral, gravado com participações de Alice Carvalho, Bento Assumpção, Gracê Passô, Liniker, Rubi, Tetê Espíndola e Thalma de Freitas. Alice Carvalho tambassina texto escrito para a edição em LP.

A produção musical do álbum “Anelis e o favo favorito” foi orquestrada pela própria Anelis Assumpção em parceria com Curumin, Ed Trombone e Saulo Duarte, este também parceiro da artista na composição de várias músicas do disco.

“Anelis e o favo favorito” chega ao mundo 15 anos após o primeiro álbum solo da cantora, “Sou suspeita, estou sujeita, não sou santa” (2011), ao qual se seguiram “Anelis Assumpção e os amigos imaginários” (2014), “Taurina” (2018) e “Sal” (2022).

articles.title: Rajpal Yadav breaks down as Bollywood bids farewell to Sanjay Gupta, says death is 'shocking... no words'
articles.summary: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta, known for 'Kaante', 'Shootout at Lokhandwala' and 'Kaabil', was cremated on October 31 after his sudden death, which has left the
articles.body: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta, known for 'Kaante', 'Shootout at Lokhandwala' and 'Kaabil', was cremated on October 31 after his sudden death, which has left the film industry in shock. He reportedly died following a fall at his Versova residence. Colleagues and friends from the industry visited his home earlier in the day to pay their respects. Among them were Abhishek Bachchan, Manoj Bajpayee, Ronit Roy, Fardeen Khan, Farah Khan, Gulshan Grover, Milap Zaveri, Jaaved Jaaferi and Harshvardhan Rane. Rajpal Yadav said he was still struggling to accept the news.Rajpal Yadav reacts to Sanjay Gupta’s sudden deathRajpal struggled to find the right words while speaking to ANI, as colleagues from the film industry gathered to bid Gupta a final goodbye. His reaction mirrored the sorrow felt across Bollywood. Fighting back tears, Yadav said, “It is a tragic loss and difficult to understand. Everyone is incredibly sad. It is really unexpected, and there are simply no words for it. For someone to pass away at such a young age is just beyond words. May God grant peace to his soul and strength to his entire family. We could never imagine this kind of news.”How Sanjay Gupta was found dead at his Mumbai homeSanjay was discovered dead at his Mumbai home, reportedly after a fall late on the night of Friday, October 30. Police have filed an accidental death report and are looking into how it happened. According to the police, he sustained a serious head injury. The matter was reported the following morning, and he was subsequently declared dead. DCP North Zone-1 Purushottam Karad confirmed that Versova Police Station was informed about the filmmaker’s death and had logged an accidental death case.Sanjay Gupta’s family raises no suspicion, say policeAccording to police, the family raised no suspicions and did not lodge any complaint regarding how the incident occurred. A post-mortem examination has been started, and the investigation into the case is ongoing.Sanjay Gupta’s journey as a directorGupta began his career as a director with 'Aatish: Feel the Fire' in 1994. Over the years, he helmed several other films, including 'Kaante', 'Musafir', 'Zinda', 'Shootout at Wadala', 'Jazbaa' and 'Mumbai Saga'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'People are actually paying for it': Ritika Singh exposes fake Facebook account using her name; warns fans against Rs 400 subscription
articles.summary: Actor Ritika Singh has cautioned her followers against a Facebook page allegedly operating under her name and collecting money through paid subscriptions.
articles.body: Actor Ritika Singh has cautioned her followers against a Facebook page allegedly operating under her name and collecting money through paid subscriptions. The account reportedly charges users Rs 400 every month, despite having no official association with the actress. Ritika Singh addressed the issue through an Instagram video, explaining how people could mistake the page for an authentic account.She clarified that her verified Instagram profile is her only official social media account. The actress also raised concerns about AI-generated deepfake videos circulating in her name.Ritika Singh identifies fake Facebook page charging Rs 400Ritika Singh said she recently discovered a Facebook page using her identity to attract subscribers. According to the actress, the account operates through a monthly payment model and has already attracted people willing to pay for its content.She pointed out that the page does not carry a verification badge. Its creators have also misspelled her name, which she believes should alert users to its questionable authenticity. The actress urged people to check account details before making payments or subscribing to profiles claiming to represent celebrities.Actress clarifies which social media account is officialIn her Instagram video, Ritika Singh directly addressed the confusion surrounding the impersonating page. She emphasized that her verified profile is the only account she personally uses to share updates and content.“I am sharing this video to make it clear that the profile you are currently seeing is my only official account. This is my only verified account with a blue tick. Everything posted here is shared by me. However, I recently came across another page on Facebook that has been created in my name. They are running it on a subscription model, charging Rs 400 a month. People are actually paying for it. The page is not verified, and they have not even spelt my name correctly. Those who are paying for it should be a little more careful with their money,” she said in her Instagram video.Ritika Singh asks followers to report suspicious pageThe actress explained that she decided to speak publicly because she did not want her followers to continue believing the Facebook page was genuine. She also deliberately avoided sharing its link. According to her, promoting the account further could draw more attention to the people operating it.Instead, Ritika Singh asked users to exercise caution whenever they encounter profiles claiming to represent her. She also requested followers to report the suspicious Facebook page. The appeal was aimed at helping prevent further confusion and potentially getting the account taken down.Coming to her work front, Ritika Singh first gained recognition through her performance in the Tamil film 'Irudhi Suttru'. She subsequently appeared in projects across Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam cinema. Her most recent project in Malayalam is Dulquer Salmaan's 'King of Kotha'. articles.title: Telangana labour department issues notice to Ravi Teja starrer ‘Irumudi’ makers over child actor Nakshathra’s working conditions
articles.summary: The makers of Ravi Teja starrer ‘Irumudi’ have received a notice from the Telangana labour department over a complaint concerning child actor Baby
articles.body: The makers of Ravi Teja starrer ‘Irumudi’ have received a notice from the Telangana labour department over a complaint concerning child actor Baby Nakshathra’s participation in the film’s shooting and promotional activities. According to the updates, the makers are now set to meet the department next week.According to Telangana Today, a meeting with the production house, Mythri Movie Makers, has been scheduled for November 4 at Anjaiah Karmika Samkshema Bhavan in RTC X Roads.Complaint raises questions about working conditionsThe complaint was reportedly filed by C Mahesh Babu, founder-president of Jai Lok Satta (Social Justice Forum). It raises concerns about Nakshathra’s working hours, remuneration and other aspects of her participation in the film.The joint commissioner of labour for the Ranga Reddy Zone has summoned the production house to attend the meeting with the relevant records.The department is also expected to examine whether the conversations and language used during a promotional event affected the child actor’s dignity and safety.Producers asked to submit documentsThe labour department has reportedly sought documents relating to permission from the District Magistrate, parental consent, attendance, working hours, educational arrangements and safety measures for Nakshathra. The producers have also been asked to submit records of the child actor’s participation in promotional activities and details of whether 20% of her remuneration was deposited in a fixed deposit account in her name.About ‘Irumudi’In ‘Irumudi’, Ravi Teja plays Trinadh, an alcoholic father who decides to undertake Ayyappa Deeksha for his daughter, Manikanta, played by Baby Nakshathra. As part of the Deeksha, he must give up his vices and remain non-violent. However, he faces a difficult situation when he has to protect the girls in his village.The film also features Priya Bhavani Shankar, Sai Kumar, Sunil, Ramesh Indira and Swasika Vijay. GV Prakash Kumar has composed the music.Upon its release, ‘Irumudi’ turned out to be a huge hit as it collected Rs 224.42 crore in India gross and worldwide gross to Rs 246.87 crore as per trade analyst Sacnilk.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Itlu Arjuna’: Nagarjuna confirms release date of Anish and Anaswara Rajan starrer romance drama after delay
articles.summary: Actors Anish and Anaswara Rajan are gearing up for the Telugu romantic entertainer ‘Itlu Arjuna’ directed by Mahesh Uppala.
articles.body: Actors Anish and Anaswara Rajan are gearing up for the Telugu romantic entertainer ‘Itlu Arjuna’ directed by Mahesh Uppala. The film was earlier set to release on October 30 was delayed, avoiding the clash with Venkatesh and Trivikram Srinivas’ ‘Adarsha Kutumbam – House No. 47’. Now the makers have announced the new release date.Nagarjuna announces ‘Itlu Arjuna’ release dateTollywood star Nagarjuna, who is presenting the film, shared the new release date on X. He also praised the young team’s passion and expressed confidence in the film’s love story.The film will now arrive in theatres on November 13, 2026.Nagarjuna wrote, “Watch out for #ItlluArjuna..!! Very happy to present this film. I’m amazed by the passion and fire of this young team! I’m sure Arjun’s love story will resonate with audiences in theatres from NOVEMBER 13th.”‘Itlu Arjuna’ marks the directorial debut of Mahesh Uppala and introduces Anish as a lead actor, with Anaswara Rajan playing the female lead.It is suggested that Anish plays a young man with speech and hearing impairments. The film’s romantic storyline and the chemistry between the lead pair have drawn attention ahead of its release. However, the makers have yet to reveal the complete story or officially confirm all the character details.Makers previously announced the delayWhen the film’s original release was postponed, the makers shared a message explaining the decision and asking audiences to continue supporting the team.They wrote, “We regret to inform that #ItlluArjuna will not be arriving on October 30th as planned. A new release date will be announced very very soon!! Until then, we seek your continued love and support for this young team. Rest assured, Arjun's love will be heard in theatres with a double bang! King @iamnagarjuna presents A @MusicThaman musical.”‘Itlu Arjuna’ technical teamTalking about the technical team of the film, S. Thaman is composing the music for Itlu Arjuna, while Raja Mahadev has handled cinematography. Ram Kumar A is the production designer, and Koti K is responsible for editing. The film’s action sequences have been choreographed by Dilip Subbarayan.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: 'Ramayana' actor Saurabh Sachdeva says online criticism doesn't bother him; calls film well-made; says religious sentiments make reactions sensitive
articles.summary: Actor Saurabh Sachdeva says he is not bothered by the online chatter and public scrutiny surrounding the much-anticipated film, \"Ramayana\", as the makers
articles.body: Actor Saurabh Sachdeva says he is not bothered by the online chatter and public scrutiny surrounding the much-anticipated film, "Ramayana", as the makers made it with a lot of care and authenticity.The film, billed as an ambitious global-scale adaptation of the Indian epic, features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita and Yash as Ravana. It is directed by Nitesh Tiwari of "Dangal" fame.After the release of the trailer, the film has received criticism over the visual effects and casting choices, including Kapoor's portrayal of Lord Ram.Sachdeva, known for featuring in films such as "Animal", "Eko" and "Pushpa 2: The Rule", among others, said the team knew religious subjects could evoke stronger reactions from people."It doesn't affect me. Now, people have a forum or place to talk about, they can say anything. If you are not getting the story and emotion right, then you can talk about not liking the film."Here (with 'Ramayana') definitely our belief is also connected, religious belief, religious sentiment is there, that is what is a little fragile. Hence, many times people will get up strongly and talk," Sachdeva told PTI in an interview.The actor said he "isn't scared". "I think the film is well-made, nothing has been added just to add, or we've not done anything just for the sake of it. Whatever I've seen, while dubbing for the film, I feel it is done in a beautiful and right way," he said.Sachdeva essays the role of the complex character Maricha in the mythological epic."I don't know how much of a villain Maricha is. He is on the villain side, but he is always in a dilemma about where to stand," he said.The actor lauded the film's director Tiwari, whom he described as a "calm and soft-spoken man"."He doesn't get agitated or upset. I haven't seen him screaming at anyone, he is a very relaxed person. He often says, 'You can do this, you can do that'."So, his calmness is very contagious, if the director is relaxed, then I'm also relaxed, and I don't have to be worried about it. I don't have to do anything."When asked about his expectations from part one of "Ramyana" on his career, Sachdeva said he hopes the film brings him more work."I hope I'll get a few more years (to work in the industry), more films, and that people will come to me. I think I will be known to Hollywood people also," he said."I feel that it will be a big hit, people will get to know more about me, more masses, and I'll get more films to do, and I'll entertain more fans," he added.Actors Arun Govil, Kunal Kapoor, Rakul Preet Singh, Lara Dutt, and Ravie Dubey round out the cast of the film.The first instalment of "Ramayana" is scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on November 5, 2026, while the second part is expected to arrive during Diwali 2027.The film will be released in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam languages.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Guys, please respect Dilip and my privacy': Farah Khan REACTS to viral video of argument with cook Dilip
articles.summary: Farah Khan has spoken out after a video showing an apparently heated exchange between her and her longtime cook, Dilip, circulated on social media.
articles.body: Farah Khan has spoken out after a video showing an apparently heated exchange between her and her longtime cook, Dilip, circulated on social media. The footage triggered discussions among viewers, with several people questioning what had happened between the two. Responding to the speculation, the filmmaker asked people to respect their privacy and avoid reaching conclusions based on a short clip.Farah Khan responds to speculationFarah Khan addressed the discussion through an Instagram post. She made it clear that people should not draw conclusions about her relationship with Dilip based on the circulating footage. The filmmaker also requested that viewers respect their personal space."Guys, please respect Dilip and my privacy. Do not jump to any conclusion (folded hands)," she wrote.Her response came after the video gained traction online. The clip shows Farah Khan and Dilip exchanging words in what appears to be a tense conversation. However, the footage does not establish what led to the disagreement.What happens in the viral video?In the video, Dilip is heard telling Farah Khan, "Maine kitni baar aapko bola hai." She responds, "Tu mujhe samjhayega?" The exchange has drawn attention because viewers are more accustomed to seeing the two share light-hearted moments in the kitchen.Farah Khan also appears to notice that someone is recording their conversation. She then asks the person behind the camera to stop filming. The brief footage has since prompted speculation about the circumstances surrounding their interaction.Neither the circulating clip nor the filmmaker's Instagram message provides further details about what happened before the exchange. Farah Khan's request, meanwhile, specifically asks viewers not to arrive at conclusions without knowing the full context.Dilip becomes a familiar face through Farah's vlogDilip is no longer just a behind-the-scenes member of Farah Khan's household. His appearances in her YouTube cooking videos have made him a recognizable personality among regular viewers. Their conversations often feature playful disagreements, sarcastic remarks and spontaneous humour.His straightforward personality and witty responses have become an important part of the videos.Farah Khan launched her cooking series on YouTube in 2024. The format brings together food preparation, celebrity appearances and conversations inside her kitchen. Rather than focusing exclusively on recipes, the videos also give viewers a glimpse of her interactions with guests.Their on-screen camaraderie draws attentionThe filmmaker's easy rapport with Dilip has remained one of the recurring attractions of her cooking videos. Their banter often provides some of the most entertaining moments, with Dilip's dry humour complementing Farah Khan's playful approach.On the work front, Farah Khan's last directorial was 'Happy New Year'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Hrithik Roshan wishes Saba Azad on her 40th birthday with heartfelt 'layover' note: 'I’d pick the 2nd option every time'
articles.summary: Hrithik Roshan and Saba Azad have been together for five years, and the pair is never shy about expressing their affection in public.
articles.body: Hrithik Roshan and Saba Azad have been together for five years, and the pair is never shy about expressing their affection in public. Having marked their fifth anniversary on October 1, Hrithik has now shared another special post for Saba. The actor wrote a sweet, heartfelt note for his girlfriend on social media as she turned 40 on November 1. In his Instagram post, Hrithik said that with her, every departure from the “normal inevitability” turns into a dance adventure.Hrithik Roshan’s flight analogy for Saba AzadSharing a post on Instagram, Hrithik wrote, “Someone asked me about you. I said I don’t wanna talk about you cause it’s too precious. She insisted and I said this .. “Well, how about this? Say if there were 2 options for flights from mumbai to a far off destination , one was a direct flight. Efficient and easy!”.Hrithik Roshan looks forward to a ‘lifetime of long layovers’The actor then described the second option: a flight out of Mumbai that stops in eight random cities, with hours of waiting at each one and a risk of missing the connection every time. “If it was with her... I said, I’d pick the 2nd option... deliberately... every single time,” he added. Concluding his note, Hrithik said he looks forward to a ‘lifetime fo long layovers’ with his girlfriend. “I love you. Happy Birthday,” he mentioned.His post begins with a close-up of Saba, and the second slide has a funny video of her. In the third, the couple share a playful boomerang, and the following three slides show the actress looking happy. The seventh and eighth slides are cheerful, candid moments of the two together. The last slide features Saba smiling alongside Hrithik’s sons, Hrehaan Roshan and Hridaan Roshan, from his first marriage to Sussanne Khan.Hrithik Roshan’s work frontOn the work front, Hrithik was last seen in a special appearance in Rajinikanth’s 'Jailer 2', directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, which was a big success at the box office. Prior to that, he had a cameo in 'Alpha', starring Alia Bhatt, Sharvari and Bobby Deol. Before both of these, he appeared in 'War 2' alongside Jr NTR and Kiara Advani. Up next, he will both direct and star in 'Krrish 4'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: 'La 1' supera a 'Antena 3' y se convierte en la televisión líder de España: la más vista de un mes de octubre desde 2011
articles.standfirst: El presidente de RTVE ha celebrado en redes sociales este hito con un mensaje claro: "No era imposible"
articles.summary: El presidente de RTVE ha celebrado en redes sociales este hito con un mensaje claro: "No era imposible"
articles.body: 'La 1' de Televisión Española (TVE) ha protagonizado uno de los cambios más destacables del panorama televisivo reciente al coronarse como la cadena más vista de España durante el pasado mes de octubre de 2026. Con un crecimiento de un punto respecto al periodo anterior, el canal público ha alcanzado un destacado 13% de cuota de pantalla, un registro que no lograba dominar en este mes específico desde el año 2011. Este éxito no se debe a un único acierto aislado, sino a una estrategia transversal consolidada en todas las franjas horarias. 'La 1' se ha erigido como líder indiscutible de la mañana con un 18,8%, de la tarde alcanzando el 10,8% y, de manera muy significativa, del codiciado prime time con un 13%, demostrando una sólida fidelización de la audiencia a lo largo de toda la jornada. Por su parte, 'Antena 3' ha cerrado el mes de octubre con un 12,5% de cuota de pantalla media siendo la primera entre las televisiones privadas aunque por detrás de la cadena pública. Eso sí, Antena 3 Noticias continúa siendo uno de sus mayores pilares y el informativo más visto de la televisión con un 24% de cuota de pantalla. 'Telecinco' sufre aunque se mantiene terera con un 8,5%, seguida de 'Cuatro' con un 7,5%, 'La Sexta' con un 5,5% y 'La 2' con un 3,3% de cuota de pantalla. Desde RTVE han celebrado la noticia con entusiasmo, una alegría que ha sido personificada en José Pablo López, presidente de la corporación, y que ha recordado que este hito histórico demuestra que el objetivo nunca fue una quimera: "No era imposible. Somos la primera cadena del país". El tirón de la programación ha sabido conectar con una amplia y diversa masa de espectadores, desbancando a sus principales competidores privados y reconfigurando el mapa de preferencias de la audiencia española. Este liderazgo refuerza el papel del ente público en un entorno de máxima competencia. La dirección y los rostros visibles de la cadena han querido trasladar un mensaje de profundo reconocimiento hacia los espectadores que han confiado en sus contenidos. Con un escueto pero sincero "Gracias", la cadena cierra un mes dorado que marca un punto de inflexión en su trayectoria reciente.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Pedro Pascal: "I always say rejection is redirection, rejection is protection. And it worked out in the end," a gentle nudge to trust the process and keep going
articles.summary: Actor Pedro Pascal shares a powerful message about rejection and opportunity, encouraging us to trust the process of life. His journey highlights how setbacks can lead to unexpected success and reminds us that everyone experiences disappointments on their path to success.
articles.body: Not every opportunity we lose is a setback. Sometimes a job rejection, a failed audition or a plan that falls through nudges us towards something we hadn’t even considered. Disappointment is hard to sit with in the moment, but looking back, you can sometimes see that a different path was waiting all along. Actor Pedro Pascal shared a thought that captures this feeling really well.Today’s quote of the day by Pedro Pascal reads: “I always say rejection is redirection, rejection is protection. And it worked out in the end.”What does Pedro Pascal’s quote mean?Pascal said this in a May 2024 interview with GQ, while talking about an audition he did for the HBO series ‘Looking’ in early 2013. He didn’t get the part, but the experience eventually pointed him towards other opportunities. Pedro Pascal's next big break came when he landed a role in Narcos, and that ended up being a real turning point for his career.Pedro's story is basically a reminder to cut yourself some slack when things don't go to plan. Rejection has a way of knocking your confidence, and it's super easy to start feeling like everyone else is zooming ahead while you're stuck in the same place. But one letdown doesn't mean your chances are gone. Sometimes life just takes a detour, and there's still loads of room for good stuff to turn up.Imagine someone who puts everything into landing their dream job and doesn't get it. Ouch, right? Especially after weeks of prepping and crossing fingers. But that sting can also be the push they needed to level up their skills, try a different route, or stumble into a place where they actually feel at home.Why does Pedro Pascal's message still matter today?People love sharing their wins, promotions and happy moments, but they rarely talk about the disappointments that came first. That can make it seem like everyone else is moving ahead while you’re still trying to find your way.Pascal's story is a good reminder that everybody gets there in their own time. Maybe you didn't get into the college you were dreaming of. Maybe you bombed a few auditions in a row, or got passed over for that promotion you were so sure about. It stings when things don't go the way you pictured, no doubt about it.His words also nudge us to separate our self-worth from other people’s decisions. Not getting picked doesn’t automatically mean you lack talent or potential. Sometimes the timing, the requirements or the circumstances just don’t line up.Pedro Pascal’s early lifeJose Pedro Balmaceda Pascal was born on April 2, 1975, in Santiago, Chile. His family left the country when he was an infant because of the political situation under the military dictatorship of Augusto Pinochet. They eventually settled in the United States, and Pascal grew up in Texas and California.He got interested in acting at a young age and studied at the Orange County School of the Arts. He later went to New York University’s Tisch School of the Arts, where he trained in drama.It wasn’t an overnight success story. Before he became a familiar face on television, Pascal spent years going to auditions, performing in theatre and taking smaller roles.How did Pedro Pascal rise to fame?Pedro Pascal's career didn't start with a big splash. He spent years picking up small TV roles, popping up in shows like Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Law & Order, and doing theatre on the side. He just kept showing up and taking whatever came his way, slowly carving out a spot for himself. For a long time, though, hardly anyone really noticed him.That finally changed in 2014, when he turned up as Oberyn Martell in season four of Game of Thrones. Viewers latched onto the character almost immediately, and it gave Pascal the breakthrough he'd been chasing for ages. People couldn't stop talking about his performance, and suddenly he had fans all over the world.He went on to play DEA agent Javier Pena in ‘Narcos’ and later became hugely popular as the title character in ‘The Mandalorian’. His turn as Joel in the drama series ‘The Last of Us’ strengthened his standing even further and earned him major award nominations.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ranbir Kapoor says India “did it 5,000 years ago” as he compares Ramayana’s Pushpaka Vimana to Elon Musk’s flying car
articles.summary: 'Ramayana' is set to release next week, and all eyes are on the film. As the release nears, the cast has been out promoting it.
articles.body: 'Ramayana' is set to release next week, and all eyes are on the film. As the release nears, the cast has been out promoting it. Ranbir Kapoor, Ravie Dubey, Rakul Preet Singh, Yash and director Nitesh Tiwari came together for an interview to discuss the journey of adapting the epic for the screen.Ranbir Kapoor on Elon Musk’s flying car and ancient IndiaDuring the chat with Star Talks, the host remarked on how remarkable the weapons of that era were, saying they could rival modern inventions, and she also praised the VFX by Academy Award-winning studio DNEG (Double Negative). Nitesh said it was wonderful to reimagine those creations on screen. Ranbir chipped in, “Elon Musk recently invented a flying car. I think India did it 5,000 years ago!”.What is the Pushpaka Vimana in 'Ramayana'The Pushpaka Vimana is a mythical self-propelled aerial chariot, or flying palace, described in the Hindu epic 'Ramayana'. It was among the visuals that stood out in the trailer, appearing as a massive flying structure.How 'Ravana' got the Pushpaka VimanaAccording to Hindu mythology, Vishwakarma, the celestial architect, built the Vimana for Lord Brahma, who then presented it to Kubera, the god of wealth and Ravana’s half-brother. Ravana, however, seized it from Kubera after defeating him. The epic describes the Pushpaka Vimana as a flying palace that travels at the speed of thought and can expand to hold any number of passengers.'Ramayana' cast, crew and release dateNitesh Tiwari’s 'Ramayana' is a two-part big-screen adaptation of the ancient Indian epic. Ranbir Kapoor stars as Lord Rama, with Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Sunny Deol appears as Lord Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. Namit Malhotra and Yash produce the film, and the music is composed by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer. The first part will hit theatres on November 5, timed with Diwali.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Kajol sends heartfelt birthday greetings to Aishwarya Rai Bachchan
articles.summary: Bollywood star Aishwarya Rai Bachchan turned a year older on Sunday.
articles.body: Bollywood star Aishwarya Rai Bachchan turned a year older on Sunday. Marking her 53rd birthday, her fans and several members of the film industry dropped adorable wishes for her on social media.Taking to Instagram, actress Kajol wrote, "Happy birthday Aishwarya...killing it on every stage."She also shared a stunning picture of Aishwarya, clicked against the iconic backdrop of the Eiffel Tower.A fan wrote on X, "Birthday wishes to former Miss World, one of the most beautiful actresses in the world."Fashion designer Manish Malhotra also extended his best wishes to Aishwarya."Dearest gorgeous. Happiest birthday. Lots of Love," he wrote.Another fan on X posted, "The face Card that has NEVER declined. The Eyes that launched a million Crushes. The Beauty that made the Entire world Stop and Stare. Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, you will ALWAYS be that Girl! From ruling Beauty pageants to owning Bollywood Screens and serving unforgettable looks at Cannes, Aishwarya has been setting standards long before social media even existed. She gave us iconic Characters, legendary songs, breathtaking dance performances and fashion moments that are still talked about today. And the best part? Her grace, confidence and elegance remain unmatched. Some people follow trends, while others become the standard. Aishwarya has always belonged to the second category."Happy Birthday to the OG Bollywood beauty queen! One face, countless iconic moments and a legacy that will never fade."Aishwarya Rai Bachchan is a fashionista, and there's no doubt about that. The first Indian woman to be crowned Miss World was Reita Faria in 1966, and after her, it took us 28 years to have another Indian beauty win it again. Aishwarya Rai ended that hiatus in the most graceful way after she brought the crown home in 1994.She made her acting debut with director MRatnam's Tamil political drama 'Iruvar' in 1997, and after that she was seen in many big Hindi films like 'Devdas', 'Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam', 'Mohabbatein', 'Guru', 'Jodhaa Akbar', 'Taal' and many more.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Congress can save America’s unique history and boost the economy with just one move
articles.summary: Trump urged Congress to pass a federal film tax credit as the U.S. share of global production has dropped from 65% to 39%, threatening American jobs.
articles.body: One of us represents historic American studios that develop and distribute the world’s greatest films and TV shows. Another represents 1.3 million hardworking Americans, including tens of thousands of drivers, transportation professionals, casting directors, animal wranglers and location scouts who are vital to the entertainment industry. And the third represents nearly 170,000 highly skilled behind-the-scenes workers who bring these stories to life. At times we’re on opposite sides of the table, but we share a north star: to grow and maintain a thriving American film and television business that creates good jobs and boosts local communities nationwide. We stand together today urging Congress to pass a long-overdue federal film incentive this year and to join us in protecting American jobs that keep our nation at the forefront of visual storytelling. The film and TV industry has always been an American economic engine, generating over 2 million jobs nationwide every year. These production jobs impact and support more than 162,000 businesses across all 50 states. The industry pays over $200 billion in wages to U.S. workers each year and holds a trade surplus with nearly every nation on Earth. HOLLYWOOD STAR SOUNDS ALARM OVER DISAPPEARING JOBS AS PRODUCTIONS FLEE CALIFORNIA When a national poll asked Americans what the U.S. does better than anyone else in the world, the top answer wasn't tech or finance, music or sports. It was movies and TV. Work in this space is a national occupation, taking advantage of unbeatable locations — from Montana’s big skies to Hawaii’s blue waters. In recent years, many states have established highly effective tax incentive programs to make local shooting even more competitive. It’s easy to see why: an average feature film adds $22 million to the economy where it shoots and a TV series production can be expected to hire 1,800 workers a season. PELOSI, OMAR JOIN TRUMP AND SCHIFF AS UNLIKELY ALLIANCE PUSHES TO ONSHORE KEY INDUSTRY Congress must build on this success by enacting a federal tax incentive that will boost production and lift up workers in every state. Republicans and Democrats collectively recognize that other nations have long been taking advantage of similar tax incentives to attract these projects and jobs. As a result of more than 120 jurisdictions around the world offering production incentives, the U.S. share of global production has slipped from a historic 65% benchmark to just 39% today. This significant decline isn’t an abstract statistic — it translates into dark soundstages, unreliable paychecks and fewer good-paying American jobs from coast to coast. PARAMOUNT ESCALATES THREAT TO LEAVE CALIFORNIA AS DEM AG'S ANTITRUST LAWSUIT STALLS WARNER BROS MERGER A federal film tax incentive will ensure America reclaims its production leadership by making domestic shoots cost-competitive. And the results will be profound. A new study found that returning the U.S. to its historic 65% share of global production would add almost $250 billion to local economies and create more than 143,000 additional jobs per year. A separate look at film and TV production decision-making found that this type of program would make 80% of the projects competitive to shoot here at home. FILM PRODUCER SAYS 'MADE IN AMERICA' MOVIES CAN HELP REVIVE HOLLYWOOD'S STRUGGLING INDUSTRY States that have had programs in place for years prove tax incentives quickly pay for themselves. One study found that the Georgia film tax credit delivers a 6.3-to-1 "return on investment" by generating new economic activity. Another determined Texas adds $4.50 to the local economy for every dollar invested in the state’s incentive. The federal government already backs strategically important industries with similarly targeted incentives to keep American jobs in America, from pharma to aerospace and automobiles. The film and television industry should be no different. Research shows that after watching American-made movies and shows, foreign audiences are significantly more likely to want to visit the U.S., buy American products and engage with American culture and history. This tangible global impact benefits each of us every day. Congress must build on this success by enacting a federal tax incentive that will boost production and lift up workers in every state. We are grateful for President Donald Trump’s leadership on prioritizing and protecting American jobs in this industry. This urgent effort was boosted by the president’s recent call for Congress to "approve, immediately, a Federal Production Incentive to create Entertainment Jobs in America." CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION We strongly support the president’s call and commend the bipartisan coalition of congressional allies for introducing the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act in the U.S. Senate and House, including Sens. Tim Scott, R-S.C., and Adam Schiff, D-Calif., as well as Reps. Nathaniel Moran, R-Texas, Linda Sánchez, D-Calif., Brian Jack, R-Ga., and Laura Friedman, D-Calif., along with the more than 50 bipartisan sponsors. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP America has long led the world in film and television production. For more than a century, it has been inherently woven into our shared American identity. We must never sacrifice our leadership, innovation or pride of ownership. There are countless more stories to tell, and we remain confident that this industry’s brightest days are yet to be imagined. But Congress must first do its job to ensure every American impacted by this essential industry can get back to work.
